newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sentrachem reinstated on S.Africa JSE Tues.
newsitem.headline: Sentrachem reinstated on S.Africa JSE Tues.

text.p: The Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) said that chemical firm Sentrachem Ltd's listing will be reinstated on the bourse from the start of trading on Tuesday.
"The reinstatement of Sentrachem will take place from the commencement of business today," a JSE spokeswoman said.

Sentrachem's shares were suspended by the JSE on Monday pending an announcement from the firm, but U.S. chemicals giant Dow Chemical Co announced later that it had offered to buy Sentrachem at 10.50 rand a share, valuing it at more than two billion rand.
Dow said it had already sealed an agreement from Sankorp Ltd, which holds 38.74 percent of Sentrachem, to accept and recommend the offer.
Dealers said Sentrachem shares, which finished at 792 cents on Friday, were likely to trace up to the 10.50 rand offer level.

The offer follows a poor performance from Sentrachem at the halfway stage, when one-off charges of 261 million rand due to forward cover contracts and restructuring costs at unit Sanachem plunged the group into a pre-tax loss of 257 million rand.
The group has since embarked on a major restructure to improve efficiencies and cut costs.
Dow is the world's fifth largest chemicals company with annual sales of more than $20 billion, about 40,000 employees and customers in 157 countries.
